question.text: When an air bubble of radius $r$ rises from the bottom to the surface of a lake, its radius becomes $\frac{5 \mathrm{r}}{4}$. Taking the atmospheric pressure to be equal to $10 \mathrm{~m}$ height of water column, the depth of the lake would approximately be (ignore the surface tension and the effect of temperature):

solution.text:
Using $\mathrm{P}_1 \mathrm{~V}_1=\mathrm{P}_2 \mathrm{~V}_2$
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\left(P_1\right) \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3=\left(P_2\right) \frac{4}{3} \pi \frac{125 r^3}{64} \\
&\frac{\rho g(10)+\rho g h}{\rho g(10)}=\frac{125}{64} \\
&640+64 h=1250
\end{aligned}
$$
On solving we get $h=9.5 \mathrm{~m}$
